text.text: AI needs an organization around it
Intelligence alone does not run a business.

Work needs authority to act, persistent state,
access to tools and an accountable execution record.

We build that operating infrastructure, then use it
to create businesses on a shared technical foundation.

text.text: Work becomes an accountable execution loop
A local harness carries a task from proposal through admission and execution—then retains the result or an explicit uncertain effect.
Implemented: capability gate, tool / worker paths and Chronicle receipts.
Native interface fixture—illustrates the harness surface, not a live workload.

text.text: A shared action layer across services

Discover a capability. Inspect its contract.
Execute it through a common interface.

Composed workflows, events,
federation and service adapters

Reusable connections for
each new organization

scenes.title: Intelligence and organizational memory
scenes.notes: Router/Chimera: bounded model dispatch, provider lanes and metering. GraphSub: connected state, persistence and query primitives. Public links: https://router.distributed.systems and https://github.com/arthurcolle/graphsub. Status: scoped component evidence, not a production-scale guarantee.

text.text:
Select how a request runs
across available models.

Bounded dispatch, provider lanes,
metering and accounting

Retain connected state
across tasks and agents.

Rust graph engine, queries and
persistence. Explicit world artifacts.
Components are implemented. Production-scale performance remains a separate validation milestone.

text.text: A proving ground for organization-shaped work
HEAT connects weather and market observations to bounded research and operations. It is an application of the shared stack—not the whole company.

scenes.notes: Founder YC pitch https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YUNJ2eLQWhw 00:57-01:11 and 02:01-02:31. Website offers scoped six-month project engagements. Future application/spinout economics are strategy, not contracted recurring revenue or completed spinouts.

text.text: Distributed Systems owns the shared infrastructure

Customer work funds development
and exposes real operating needs.

The same tools, harness and state
serve subsequent deployments.

Develop and spin out businesses
while retaining the underlying stack.
